title: The Space Elevator
description: A cable from the equator to beyond geostationary orbit, held taut by the Earth's spin: climbers ride it up with no rocket at all. The cable must hold its own weight, so it tapers, thickest at the top; the taper ratio grows as exp(ρgR²/σr), which is hopeless for steel and possible only for nanotubes. Unlocks the Space Elevator: a second route to orbit, needing only power.

puzzle.goal: A tether of density ρ and strength σ hangs from geostationary orbit. Its taper ratio (cross-section at the top over that at the ground) is exp of the characteristic stress ratio. With the planet's surface gravity g and radius R and the geostationary radius r, write the taper ratio T.
puzzle.name: The tether taper
puzzle.form: exp ( ρ * g * R ^ 2 / ( σ * r ) )
puzzle.expr: exp ( rho * g * R ^ 2 / ( sigma * r ) )
puzzle.ask: Find T for a nanotube tether: ρ = @{rho} kg/m³, σ = @{sigma} Pa, g = 9.81 m/s², R = 6.371e6 m, r = 4.216e7 m.
puzzle.method: Constant stress σ along the tether: dA/A = (ρ/σ)·(net gravity minus centrifugal)·dr; integrate to the top.
